title: One Hand for the Smallest
style: Dark singer-songwriter ballad, intimate New England female lead with clear regional cadence and unvarnished storytelling, slow measured pulse, low piano and muted acoustic guitar, restrained cello entering beneath the verses, subtle brushed percussion only in later sections, arrangement gradually widens around the refrain then falls back to voice and piano for the closing thought, close dry vocal with natural breaths, warm grain and understated room ambience, mix keeps the words forward and avoids melodrama.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Steven Swansen, my father was a bull
That’s how I remember him, broad-backed, hard to move
Thanksgiving in Worcester, twenty-two
The next year went by with too much to do

[Verse 2]
Then came the inquiry, I left my practice behind
Surrendered my license, crossed the equator line
Bogotá, no backward glance
Dad and I kept a careful distance

[Refrain]
Once or twice a month, a message passed
If you’re generous, you could call it that
With Mom, holiday cards, birthdays on a screen
The ordinary ways we kept between

[Verse 3]
He never told me diabetes had begun
I didn’t know what it had taken, what was gone
Then came the stroke, Maureen called three days on
He was awake when she turned the camera on

[Verse 4]
I cleared my appointments, booked Logan that night
Texted Thomas and María Teresa, set things right
Índigo could wait, I thought he’d understand
“Take your time,” came back, plain as a hand

[Refrain]
Too early to tell, the doctors said
One side still quiet, one side in the bed
I knew that phrase, I’d used it myself
A careful way to set hope on a shelf

[Verse 5]
By the time I reached Worcester, he was more alert
But one arm wouldn’t answer, one side hurt
Maureen and I brought him home the following week
She had work to return to, I had time to keep

[Bridge]
I could stay, for now, while the answers took their time
A job, my savings, the edge of the line
The bull learned one hand for the smallest things
A button, a cup, the ordinary sting

[Outro]
He’s lucid, though
That helps
Well, it helps us
I’m not sure it helps him
